o.text: From yat- (“to sleep; to lie down”) + -aq. Cognate with Turkish yatak.
From Classical Persian سبک (sabk) as in سبک خراسانی (sabk-i xorāsānī) or سبک هندی (sabk-i hindi), where the izafet has been reinterpreted as part of the stem. Ultimately from Arabic سَبْك (sabk).
Borrowed from Russian скамья́ (skamʹjá), ultimately from Medieval Greek σκαμνία (skamnía).
Borrowed from Turkish önşart/ön şart, or independently calqued from English precondition. By surface analysis, ön + şərt.
Borrowed from Turkish alt yazı. By surface analysis, alt + yazı.
